abstract: Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) inhabits the persistently cold waters of the Southern Ocean, where lipid metabolism supports membrane function and energy storage. Despite extensive characterization of euphausiid lipid classes and bulk fatty acids, fatty acyl organization across lipid pools remains poorly understood. We integrated untargeted metabolomics and lipidomics to compare whole-body biochemical profiles of E. superba and its congener E. triacantha. Metabolomics revealed differences in glycerophospholipid (GP) and glycerolipid (GL) metabolism, together with alterations in pathways associated with nucleotide metabolism, redox regulation, and lipid precursor supply. Lipidomics further revealed selective remodeling at the lipid-class and molecular-species levels rather than a global increase in lipid unsaturation. Relative to E. triacantha, E. superba showed lower relative abundances of multiple lysophospholipid classes and a higher relative abundance of cardiolipin. E. superba also showed higher relative abundances of polyunsaturated glycerophospholipids, whereas a subset of predominantly polyunsaturated triacylglycerol species showed lower relative abundances. C20:5, C22:5, and C22:6 showed higher relative abundances in the GP pool but lower relative abundances in the GL pool of E. superba. Together, these findings place selective fatty acyl partitioning within an integrated metabolic framework associated with long-term cold adaptation in E. superba.
